sources.title: JTA: Israel Premier Starts Campaign for Unified System of Education
sources.evidence: Ben-Gurion advocated national schooling to build a united nation while expressly rejecting totalitarian education.

sources.title: Israel Democracy Institute: The Religious Community and the Constitution
sources.evidence: Ben-Gurion opposed an entrenched constitution superior to ordinary legislation and helped postpone it in 1950.

sources.title: JTA: Easing of Military Government for Israel Arabs Follows Knesset Debate
sources.evidence: He defended retaining military government in Arab border areas while agreeing to appeals, longer movement permits and removal of some curfews.

sources.title: JTA: Ben Gurion Presents New Economic Policy, Investors to Benefit
sources.evidence: His parliamentary economic programme encouraged foreign investment, reduced spending and introduced multiple controlled exchange rates.

sources.title: Israeli government note transmitted by Abba Eban, FRUS document 469
sources.evidence: Government promised a foreign-exchange budget, central allocation of currency and centralized import priorities while seeking US assistance and financial stabilization.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: The Suez Crisis, 1956
sources.evidence: Israel joined the secret Anglo-French plan against Egypt and invaded Sinai in October 1956; US and UN pressure forced a ceasefire.

sources.title: Kennedy–Ben-Gurion conversation, FRUS document 57
sources.evidence: Ben-Gurion linked Dimona to nuclear energy and desalination, sought advanced defensive arms and accepted neutral scientific visits in discussion with Kennedy.

sources.title: Secretary Rusk memorandum, FRUS document 5
sources.evidence: Dimona was built secretly with French support; Ben-Gurion publicly denied plans for nuclear weapons. Record supports nuclear development but not a public weapons admission.

sources.title: Ben-Gurion Heritage Institute: dated speeches and quotations
sources.evidence: 1950 Law of Return rationale prioritizes Jewish immigration; dated 1952 and 1957 speeches connect diaspora and state. 1955 Negev speech promotes scientific development; 1963 Years of Challenge stresses pioneering work.

sources.title: Library of Congress: David Ben-Gurion – The Man and His Legacy
sources.evidence: The 1955 Negev programme called for desalination, solar and wind energy, water conservation and research on desert vegetation.

sources.title: Ben-Gurion letter asking Who Is a Jew, translation held by Chabad
sources.evidence: Consulted Orthodox and non-Orthodox scholars while affirming freedom of conscience and religion and the needs of sovereign immigrant absorption.

sources.title: Center for Israel Education: Status Quo Agreement, translated document
sources.evidence: Promised Sabbath rest, kosher public kitchens, religious personal-status arrangements and educational autonomy. Pre-period commitment explains institutions retained during premiership.

sources.title: National Library of Israel: Four Decisions by David Ben-Gurion That Shaped Israel
sources.evidence: Archives describe his support of the 1951 Women’s Equal Rights Law and praise of women’s contributions to building and defending the state.

sources.title: Anat Maor: Israel Studies Anthology, Women in Israel
sources.evidence: Women’s civil equality coexisted with religious marriage and divorce jurisdiction from 1953 and Ben-Gurion’s pronatalist emphasis on motherhood.

sources.title: Fortune: Israel without ideology
sources.evidence: Ben-Gurion protected Histadrut enterprises while seeking private investment.

sources.title: US–Ben-Gurion conversation, FRUS document 132
sources.evidence: He argued that war generally fails to solve problems, while insisting on self-defense and seeking British and French arms.

sources.title: Berkeley Law Library catalogue: Rebirth and Destiny of Israel
sources.evidence: Lists Ben-Gurion as author and Nurock as editor/translator; Philosophical Library, New York, 1954, 539 pages.

sources.title: Political Science Quarterly: contemporary book review
sources.evidence: Contemporary review confirms title, Ben-Gurion authorship, Nurock translation/editing and 1954 publication.

sources.title: Open Library catalogue: Rebirth and Destiny of Israel
sources.evidence: Collection of the author’s political essays and addresses written or delivered from 1915 to 1952; supports relevance to Zionism and state formation.

facts: 1953 national education campaign sought a common nation rather than competing party school systems.
estrutura.tension: Centralized state-building left room for religious school autonomy and cooperative settlements; neither implies territorial federalism.

facts: Operated through the Knesset and electoral coalition institutions; fought constitutional entrenchment during 1949–50.
representacao.tension: Parliamentary democracy and universal civic rhetoric coexist with executive dominance and limits on Arab freedom; opposition to judicial review is not opposition to elections.

facts: In 1962 defended continuing military rule over Arab border communities, accepting only limited relaxations.
poder.tension: Distinguish security detention and curfews from an unrestricted police state; right of appeal was among accepted concessions.

facts: Law of Return promoted Jewish immigration; national schooling was explicitly intended to integrate different groups into one Israeli nation.
imigracao.tension: Mass Jewish immigration is not universal open borders; common Hebrew national identity coexists with religious pluralism. No basis to infer blanket expulsion of Jewish immigrants for retaining customs.

facts: 1956 Sinai attack and allied planning demonstrate willingness to use force; in 1961 sought arms and nuclear scientific capacity.
diplomacia.tension: Strong deterrence and preemption coexist with negotiations and the stated view that wars usually do not resolve problems; nuclear weapons endorsement is an inference, not a public admission.

facts: Joined external intervention against Egypt in 1956 and sought foreign alliances/arms to secure Israel.
intervencao.tension: Assertive regional security objectives did not amount to a general programme of global military conquest; foreign dependence also constrained action.

facts: Protected the Histadrut collective sector while inviting private foreign investment in 1952.
economia.tension: Labour Zionist cooperative development is neither universal expropriation nor market privatization; public provision need not mean every provider is central government.

facts: 1952 programme used administered exchange rates, foreign-currency allocation and import planning.
controle.tension: Spending restraint and investment incentives corrected the austerity economy without abandoning strategic direction; no support for total Soviet-style planning.

facts: Centralized import priorities in 1952 while seeking foreign capital, machinery and US assistance.
comercio.tension: Strategic domestic development and selective protection coexist with trade dependence and welcome for foreign investment, not autarky.

facts: 1947 commitments retained in office protected Sabbath, kosher institutions and religious personal status; 1958 consultation affirmed freedom of conscience.
religiao.tension: Secular national government and biblical cultural attachment coexist; neither militant atheism nor halakhic sovereignty describes him.

facts: Supported civil equality for women in 1951, but retained religious marriage jurisdiction in 1953 and promoted motherhood for national demographic goals.
moral.tension: Civic and labour equality did not entail contemporary LGBT, reproductive or polyamorous liberation. Answers to these are explicit low-confidence historical inference, not attributed quotations.

facts: 1955 Negev agenda advocated desalination and solar/wind research; 1961 nuclear programme aimed publicly at power and desalination.
tecnologia.tension: Pioneering rural settlement and water conservation coexist with industrial scientific optimism; enthusiasm for applied research does not prove unlimited human enhancement.

limitations: Historical model is exclusively state-building/premiership, 1948–1953 and 1955–1963; later private views and post-1963 political changes are excluded. The 1947 agreement is used only to explain in-period institutions.

Digital surveillance, cryptocurrencies, contemporary gender identity, genetic enhancement and climate-policy questions are analogical simulations with lower confidence; no claim of literal positions on unavailable technologies.
Several archive pages returned 403 on opening; their indexed text was usable. Knesset biography returned no text and was not treated as evidence.

No Brazilian edition of Rebirth and Destiny of Israel was verified after searches combining the English title, português, Brasil and Renascimento e destino. A machine-translated encyclopedia title was rejected as edition evidence.

The memoir Israel: A Personal History (1971 translation of a 1969 Hebrew work) was considered; the 1954 political collection is selected for its direct presentation of the formative political programme and relevance to the modeled era. An isolated review gives 1953, but the title-page-based library record and contemporary June 1954 review support 1954.

bookDecision.reason: Self-authored substantive political speeches and essays; selected for direct relevance to his formative programme. Nurock edited and translated rather than replacing the author. No existing catalogue book for this personality; proposed addition only.

processNotes: Read CONTRIBUTING.md, NEW_PROFILE.md, README.md, new-personality skill and own saved prompt. Read only own existing research period and URLs, never prior answers or vectors.
Metadata accuracy and likely neighbours were reported to coordinator before answering. Research and prompt were written before answers.

Likely neighbours without targets: Golda Meir (Labour Zionism, with Ben-Gurion distinctive founding centralization); Menachem Begin (security nationalism but different labour economics and constitutional stance); Atatürk (secular modernization but different religious compromises and electoral institutions).
Exactly one independent audit; no further delegation, no adjustment for numerical targets or similarity.
Answers were individually selected in shuffled question order; no prior answer archive, stored vector, similarity review or score report was opened before generation.
After first validation revealed the duplicate blocker, no answer was changed. Validation was rerun only to capture its exact process return code and full output in this evidence file.

Neutral reasons: immigration_10 balances cultural preservation with national integration; immigration_12 balances humanitarian admission with nationally selective immigration; diplomacia_04 balances the claim that wars seldom solve problems with actual preventive war; economia_12 balances labour security with administrative efficiency; economia_01 balances social transformation with rejection of class seizure; economia_02 balances mixed-economy pragmatism with collective provision; controle_06 balances investment incentives with national funding needs; comercio_16 balances consumer relief with industrial protection; religiao_03/05/04 balance secular civil government with institutional religious compromises; moral_11 balances secular public education with conventional family morality; moral_18 balances women’s public work with pronatal motherhood; tecnologia_10 balances water conservation with technological growth; tecnologia_04 balances research enthusiasm with ethical limits.

Archetypes chosen from their text: society D for equality and civic rights, power C as the parliamentary option despite opposition to entrenched judicial review, economy B for cooperatives/social provision/regulation, world B for strong defense and allies, technology D for industrial/scientific development.
No whole-project tests, merge, shared metadata edits, book edits, STATE edits or archival answer edits were performed.
